title: Coordinator
description:
Coordinator
Location: Eastleigh
Salary: £14.71 P/H
Hours: Monday to Friday, full-time hours
Contract: please note, this is a 12 week temporary contract.

We are currently recruiting for an organised and proactive Coordinator to join a busy operational team within an established organisation. - Monitor workloads, priorities and outstanding jobs, using internal systems and dashboards to ensure work is progressed appropriately.

- Strong attention to detail and the ability to maintain accurate records.
- A proactive, efficient and collaborative approach to work.

title: Healthy Homes Administrator & Scheduling Coordinator
description:
Healthy Homes Administrator & Scheduling Coordinator

Salary: Up to 28,310 per annum, depending on experience
Hours: 37 hours per week
Location: Eastleigh
Contract: 3 Month Fixed Term Contract

The Role

We're looking for an organised and customer-focused Healthy Homes Administrator & Scheduling Coordinator to join a busy team supporting the delivery of a high-quality disrepair service to fulfil a 3 month contract

Based at the Eastleigh office, you'll play a key role in coordinating appointments, managing operatives' and surveyors' diaries, and ensuring disrepair cases progress efficiently.

You'll be an important point of contact for customers throughout the process, keeping them informed, managing expectations and helping ensure work is coordinated effectively from initial inspection through to completion.

What You'll Be Doing

You'll help keep the Healthy Homes service running smoothly by coordinating a wide range of appointments, communications and administrative activities.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Scheduling inspections, repair appointments and follow-on works.
- Managing and coordinating operatives' and surveyors' diaries.
- Keeping customers informed about appointments, progress and changes.
- Supporting customers throughout the disrepair process.
- Coordinating activity across multiple disrepair cases.
- Liaising with customers, colleagues, surveyors, operatives, contractors and legal representatives.
- Ensuring appointments and follow-on works are arranged efficiently.
- Maintaining accurate records and updating relevant systems.
- Monitoring case progress and helping ensure actions are completed within required timescales.
- Managing changes to schedules and resolving appointment-related issues.
- Supporting the wider team with administrative tasks as required.
- Ensuring communications and records are accurate, timely and professional.

About You

We're looking for someone who is highly organised, proactive and customer-focused, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a busy environment.

You'll be someone who:
- Has excellent organisational and time-management skills.
- Is confident coordinating multiple diaries and appointments.
- Communicates clearly and professionally with customers and colleagues.
- Has strong attention to detail and maintains accurate records.
- Can manage competing priorities and work effectively to deadlines.
- Is confident dealing with changes and finding practical solutions to problems.
- Builds positive working relationships with a wide range of people.
- Remains calm and professional when dealing with challenging situations.
- Takes ownership of tasks and follows them through to completion.
- Is comfortable working as part of a busy and collaborative team.

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
TPF Recruitment is delighted to be representing one of our established clients based in Eastleigh, Hampshire, in their search for a Payroll Administrator. This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing business and develop your payroll career within a supportive team environment.

Our client provides tailored payroll services to businesses of all sizes across the UK, offering a personalised approach to meet the individual needs of each client.

As a Payroll Administrator, you will support the delivery of accurate and efficient payroll services across a varied client portfolio. Working closely with experienced colleagues, you will assist with processing weekly, fortnightly and monthly payrolls, responding to client queries and ensuring payroll deadlines are consistently met.

The business is currently experiencing an exciting period of growth, offering the successful candidate the opportunity to develop their skills and progress their career over time.

Key Responsibilities
- Process weekly, fortnightly and monthly payrolls for a diverse portfolio of clients.
- Collate and input payroll information, ensuring data is accurate and processed within the required deadlines.
- Assist with payroll reconciliations and the preparation of payroll reports.
- Support the administration of pension auto-enrolment and related submissions.
- Respond to client, HMRC and internal payroll queries in a professional and timely manner.
- Assist with the calculation of statutory payments, including SSP and statutory family leave.
- Maintain accurate payroll records and ensure relevant documentation is kept up to date.
- Support the onboarding of new clients and the setup of payroll systems.
- Work collaboratively with the wider payroll team to ensure a high standard of service.

Requirements
- Previous experience in payroll administration, ideally within an accountancy practice or payroll bureau environment.
- A good understanding of payroll processes, including PAYE, National Insurance and workplace pensions.
- Familiarity with statutory payments, including SSP and statutory family leave, would be advantageous.
- Strong numerical skills and excellent attention to detail.
- Good organisational skills, with the ability to manage workloads and meet deadlines.
- Confident communication skills, with a professional and client-focused approach.
- Competent IT skills, including Microsoft Office and Excel.
- A proactive attitude and willingness to learn and develop within a growing team.

Benefits
- Salary of £26,000 - £30,000 per annum, depending on experience.
- 25 days' annual leave plus bank holidays.
- Hybrid working opportunities.
- Flexible start and finish times.
- Exposure to a varied portfolio of clients across the UK.
- Opportunities for ongoing training, development and career progression.
